subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw support LLM-driven contextual group activation for unmentioned WhatsApp and Telegram group messages, and if so should it be a shared channel/plugin SDK contract or a channel-specific core feature?
rationale: The request changes when shared-room content reaches model providers, adds public config and fallback-model behavior, and crosses Telegram, WhatsApp, plugin, session-state, logging, and security boundaries; automation cannot safely choose that product/security contract.

options.title: Design a shared activation contract
options.body: Create a default-off, cross-channel contract for contextual activation with explicit privacy, provider, logging, and state semantics before implementing channel integrations.

options.title: Narrow to adjacent tracked work
options.body: Close or defer the full peeking/engaged design and pursue only the narrower attention-window, per-mention routing, or passive hook issues that already exist.

options.title: Reject ambient LLM peeking
options.body: Keep requireMention, always-on groups, and passive history as the supported safety model, and document that model-driven peeking is out of scope for core.

recommendation.title: Design a shared activation contract
recommendation.body: Create a default-off, cross-channel contract for contextual activation with explicit privacy, provider, logging, and state semantics before implementing channel integrations.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history signal across shared mention policy, group activation parsing, Telegram behavior, and prior group activation reviews.
